newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks edge up in dead slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks edge up in dead slow trade.

text.p: Mexican stocks inched up at the open Monday in what dealers called an extremely slow session due to the U.S. Memorial Day holiday.
Dealing was also slow as open outcry was suspended and screen trading only would be used.
"Nothing is happening, it's very dull, just screen trading and no U.S. investors. They liked the trade balance figures a little," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index .MXX was up 0.42 points in the opening minutes of trade, or 0.01 percent, at 3,988.71.
Trading volume .TV.MX stood at 1.7 million shares, of which one single cross trade accounted for one million. In total, just 18 trades had been settled.
Mexico chalked up a trade surplus of $109 million in April, the Finance Ministry announced early on Monday.

Restaurant chain ECE Corp led the short gainers' list .PG.MX, up 54 centavos to 11.26 pesos following news late on Friday the firm had jointly won bidding for a development project at the Mexico City racecourse, dealers said.
On the broad market, of eight stocks traded, four were ahead while the remaining four were unchanged.
